title: Quarterly review: metrics playground & lab notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, experimental notes doc for customer-success QBR and renewal conversations. The intent is to capture clear, repeatable metric definitions for conversations around latency, uptime, cost/token, and cache hit rate and to provide a compact KPI table and troubleshooting checklist that CSMs can adapt per account.

Audience:
CS managers, CSMs preparing QBRs, Solutions Engineers who support QBR data pulls, and PMs who want consistent signal definitions. Not intended as final policy — this is a working draft (lab notes).

High-level guidance (one-liner):
 - Use p50/p95 for day-to-day ops; surface p99 for high-sensitivity latency SLOs.
 - Uptime should be expressed as rolling 30d and 90d windows and compared to contractual SLA.
 - Cost/token should show compute + infra + request overhead normalized to tokens returned (not just model cost).
 - Cache hit rate must be broken down by prefix (prompt) vs KV cache and by effective token-savings.

Metric definitions (operational):
1) Latency (end-to-end request latency)
 - Definition: time from client request ingress (API receive timestamp) to final response bytes sent (end-of-stream). Include network ingress hop inside Redwood edge but exclude upstream customer network.
 - Percentiles: report p50, p95, p99. Use server-side trace timestamps (edge -> runtime -> response).
 - Measurement window: rolling 7d for alerts, 30d for QBR trend, 90d for historical context.
 - SLO guidance: starter customers: p95 < 450ms, growth customers: p95 < 300ms, enterprise low-latency tier: p95 < 150ms. These are soft guidance examples — use customer SLA where present.
 - Notes: show distribution by route/model, and by request length bins (<=64 tokens, 65-512, >512).

2) Uptime (availability)
 - Definition: % of successful API responses (200-level) vs total attempted requests in window, excluding planned maintenance windows (documented). Include service-level dependencies only (not 3rd-party user infra).
 - Measurement window: rolling 30d and 90d. For QBR present both.
 - SLA mapping: show observed uptime vs contractual SLA (e.g., 99.5% monthly). For incidents, annotate downtime root cause and mitigation taken.
 - Edge cases: internal retries that succeed should be counted as successful only if final response returned; if a retry leads to excess latency, that is captured under latency metric.

3) Cost per token (unit economics)
 - Definition: total billed cost divided by tokens returned in the reporting window. Token count = model output tokens + (optional) returned context tokens if customer charges include them. For CS-facing QBRs prefer normalized: cost_per_1k_output_tokens.
 - Cost components (recommended breakdown to show):
    a) Model compute (GPU time amortized)
    b) Networking & egress (if significant for large responses)
    c) Orchestration/overhead (autoscaler/idle buffer allocation amortization)
    d) Caching savings (subtractive line item showing what portion of token cost was avoided)
 - Formula examples: cost_per_token = (total_cost_usd - cache_savings_usd) / total_output_tokens. Then cost_per_1k = cost_per_token * 1000.
 - Measurement window: monthly rolling and quarter-to-date for QBR.
 - Benchmarks: small accounts often >$0.12/1k tokens (dev); optimized production customers frequently 0.5–3¢/1k tokens depending on quantization and batching.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix / KV / result cache)
 - Definition: proportion of requests that returned at least one response token from cache vs total requests. For clarity break into: prefix_cache_hit_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, response_cache_hit_rate (whole-response).
 - Effective token savings: report % of tokens served from cache (tokens_from_cache / total_tokens) in addition to hit rate. This shows real cost impact.
 - Measurement window: rolling 30d for QBR.
 - Target guidance: >35% token savings is strong for chat-heavy workloads; >60% is exceptional (long-session chat + stable prompts).
 - Notes: surface partial-cache hits (prefix only) in a separate column — they reduce compute but still require generation for remainder.

Suggested KPI table (compact):
Columns: metric | window | value | target | trend | note
Sample rows (text table):
metric | window | value | target | trend | note
latency_p95 | 30d | 312ms | <300ms | ↑ from -8% last qtr | high tail on >512 token requests
latency_p99 | 30d | 1.24s | <1s | ↔ | rare spikes correlated with autoscale events
uptime | 90d | 99.72% | 99.5% | ↓ slightly | one maintenance incident (2026-01-21)
cost_per_1k_tokens | month | $0.028 | $0.02–0.05 | ↓ | recent quantize+batch rollout
cache_token_savings_pct | 30d | 41% | >30% | ↑ | prefix cache tuning applied

Interpretation guidance (one paragraph each):
 - Latency: If p95 is within target but p99 is high, highlight tail risk and correlate with request length and burst periods; propose canarying a smaller quantized variant for tail-sensitive endpoints.
 - Uptime: If below SLA, include incident summary and remediation plan (owner + timeline). For nearing SLA breaches, recommend incrementally increasing dedicated capacity or enabling cross-region fallback.
 - Cost per token: show trend pre/post any infra changes (e.g., rounding of batch windows, quantization toggles) and call out caching gains as a separate bullet to show value captured by Redwood Optimize suggestions.
 - Cache: if effective token savings are low, run a prompt-coverage audit (common prefixes) and suggest inserting explicit cacheable templates or enabling longer session caching.

QBR deliverables checklist (for CSM):
 - Data snapshot csv attached (raw metrics by day and by route)
 - One-slide executive summary: 3 bullets (top risk, top win, ask)
 - Customer-facing KPI table (single page)
 - Action plan: 1–3 recommendations (owner + ETA)
 - Technical appendix with distribution plots and route-level breakdown

Troubleshooting checklist (quick ops cues):
 - If p95 spikes: check request length distribution, recent deploys (model variant changes), autoscale events, and edge throttles.
 - If cache hit drops: did prompt templates change? Are session IDs being forwarded correctly? Any rollout that invalidated cache key hashing?
 - If cost/unit increases suddenly: check model size swap, burst traffic (billing step-change), failed cache layer, or long tail regeneration loops.

Example short customer narrative (template to adapt):
"This quarter we observed a 41% effective token savings from caching which reduced apparent model compute cost by roughly 18% QoQ. P95 latency is 312ms (slightly above our internal target of 300ms) driven by a 12% increase in >512-token requests during product demos. We recommend a targeted canary of the 8-bit quantized variant for the demo route and a template audit to increase cacheable prefixes.
Action: SE Maya to run prompt-coverage audit (2w), CSM Diego to propose canary schedule (1w)."

Appendix: Useful queries and exports (SEs)
 - SQL-ish pseudocode to compute p95 latency per route: SELECT route, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) FROM api_traces WHERE ts BETWEEN start AND end GROUP BY route;
 - Cache token savings: SELECT sum(tokens_from_cache) / sum(total_tokens) as token_savings FROM request_cache_stats WHERE ts BETWEEN start AND end;
 - Cost breakdown by bucket: use cost center exports + allocation tags (model_variant, route, project_tag).

Open questions / lab items to iterate on:
 - Should cost/token include input tokens for customers who bill on total context? For now we present both (output-only and output+context) and recommend aligning to customer billing model for renewal conversations.
 - Explore adding a derived "time-to-first-byte" metric for streaming endpoints (useful for interactive UIs).
 - Automate a CSV export template so CSMs can paste into slide decks with one click.

Next steps (this doc):
 - Iterate with 2 pilot CSM QBRs in February 2026 and refine wording based on customer feedback.
 - Add a one-page slide template and a script for generating the KPI table from our metrics exports.

Notes to self (short):
 - keep examples small and actionable. Avoid burying execs in percentiles.
 - prioritize token-savings numbers in renewal talks (direct ROI story).

End of lab notes.
